title: NSUF awards 18 Super Rapid Turnaround Experiments
summary: The Department of Energy’s Office of Nuclear Energy has awarded National Science User Facilities (NSUF) access to 18 Super Rapid Turnaround Experiment (Super RTE) projects. The awarded facility access is valued at approximately $2.7 million. The Super RTE projects will support nuclear fuels and materials research, the deployment of new nuclear reactors, and the continued operation of existing reactors. The teams will be led by researchers from 11 institutions representing three national laboratories, seven universities, and one industry partner.

title: PNNL is developing a new approach for creating alloys
summary: Researchers at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory are designing new types of metallic alloys that can better withstand the extreme conditions of heat, radiation, and mechanical stress inside nuclear reactors. Led by materials scientist and principal investigator Osman El Atwani, the team uses an approach termed robust alloy design (RAD) that has been described in the journal Materials & Design.

title: Canada’s Bruce-5 Nuclear Plant Taken Offline For Major Component Replacement Outage
summary: The Bruce-5 nuclear power plant has been taken offline for its major component replacement (MCR) outage – the fourth unit to be refurbished under Bruce Power’s plan to renew six of the eight units at the Ontario site. The company said the 817-MW Candu pressurised heavy water reactor (PHWR) unit, which began commercial operation in 1985, was taken offline on 1 November. It said: “This represents the second half of the company’s privately backed MCR Project that will see units 3-8 renewed to provide clean, reliable energy for Ontario’s people, businesses and hospitals for decades to come, while also ensuring a dependable source of cancer-fighting medical isotopes for the world healthcare community.”

title: Amentum And Kyoto Fusioneering Sign MOU On Fusion In UK, Japan And US
summary: US engineering and energy technology company Amentum has entered into a memorandum of understanding with Kyoto Fusioneering to cooperate on nuclear fusion in the UK, Japan and the US. Amentum said the agreement with Kyoto Fusioneering, a Japan-based developer of fusion technologies, establishes a framework to strengthen both companies’ roles in advancing fusion energy commercialisation.
